title: Woman Throws Ink at CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke at Jantar Mantar Protest
excerpt: The attacker was identified as a men’s rights activist who had previously supported convicted rapist Kuldeep Singh Sengar. The incident came as activists and students intensified protests over the NEET paper leak.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • A woman threw ink at CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke during a protest at Jantar Mantar.
  • The attacker is a men's rights activist linked to convicted rapist Kuldeep Singh Sengar.
  • Dipke faced a second attack in five weeks, highlighting rising tensions in protests.
  • Sonam Wangchuk was hospitalized after 20 days of hunger strike amid NEET paper leak protests.
  • CJP plans a march to Parliament on July 20, demanding the Education Minister's resignation.
Protest Chaos at Jantar Mantar
›Ink attack on Abhijeet Dipke at 7:46 a.m. on July 18.
›Thousands gathered to protest NEET paper leak.
›Dipke previously attacked on June 15 during a protest in Jaipur.
›CJP has over 22.5 million Instagram followers.
> **"On June 15, the 30-year-old was slapped repeatedly by two men while being carried on supporters' shoulders during a protest in Jaipur."** ![Sonam Wangchuk — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f2/Sonam_Wangchuk%2C_2017_%28cropped%29.jpg)
  • A woman threw ink at Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke at Jantar Mantar on July 18, causing chaos at the protest site where thousands had gathered.
  • The attacker was identified as a men’s rights activist who had previously supported convicted rapist Kuldeep Singh Sengar, according to The Indian Express.
  • The incident occurred hours before Delhi Police forcibly moved hunger-striking activist Sonam Wangchuk to Safdarjung Hospital after 20 days of fasting.
  • The CJP has announced a march to Parliament on July 20, the opening day of the Monsoon Session, to demand Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation.

A woman threw ink at Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke at the Jantar Mantar protest site in Delhi on Friday, the second physical attack on the youth leader in just over a month as tensions around India's education crisis escalate.

The incident, which occurred around 7:46 a.m. on July 18, caused chaos at the protest site where thousands of students and supporters had gathered to demand the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak scandal. Dipke later posted on social media with the caption "Blue is my colour," according to Dainik Bhaskar.

Wangchuk's Hunger Strike
›Sonam Wangchuk hospitalized after 20 days of fasting.
›Admitted with dehydration and low potassium levels.
›Wangchuk's wife questioned the necessity of hospitalization.
›Three students also require medical attention after fasting.
https://x.com/TimesNow/status/2078555403386802496

Attacker Identified as Sengar Supporter

The woman who threw the ink was identified as a men's rights activist who had previously supported convicted rapist Kuldeep Singh Sengar, the expelled BJP MLA sentenced to life imprisonment in the 2017 Unnao rape case, according to The Indian Express. During protests in December 2025 against the Delhi High Court's decision to suspend Sengar's sentence, a woman from the men's rights organization Purush Aayog had held a placard reading "I Support Kuldeep Sengar" at the same Jantar Mantar venue, sparking a heated confrontation with the Unnao rape survivor's supporters.

The intersection of the two protest movements at the same Delhi landmark underscored the increasingly volatile atmosphere around the site, which has become the epicenter of India's largest youth-led movement in years.

Second Attack on Dipke

The ink attack was the second assault on Dipke in five weeks. On June 15, the 30-year-old was slapped repeatedly by two men while being carried on supporters' shoulders during a protest in Jaipur. The men who slapped him were later welcomed as heroes by supporters who garlanded them upon their release from police custody, according to DNA India.

Dipke, a Boston University-trained digital communications strategist, founded the satirical CJP in May 2026 after Chief Justice of India Surya Kant drew criticism for comparing certain activists and unemployed young people to "cockroaches." The movement has since amassed over 22.5 million Instagram followers and organized nationwide protests.

Wangchuk Hospitalized

The ink attack came on the same morning that Delhi Police forcibly moved education reform activist Sonam Wangchuk from the Jantar Mantar protest site to Safdarjung Hospital after 20 days of hunger strike. Wangchuk, who had been fasting to demand an investigation into the alleged NEET paper leak, was admitted with dehydration and low potassium levels but refused all medical treatment.

Wangchuk's wife, Gitanjali J. Angmo, alleged the hospitalization was unnecessary and questioned the hospital's medical findings, saying his potassium levels could not have dropped from 4.3 to 2.9 in a single day.

"In every state, in every district, set up a Jantar Mantar! And protest there just like the way it has been going on here for a month."

— Abhijeet Dipke, CJP founder

What’s Next

The CJP has announced a march to Parliament on July 20, the opening day of the Monsoon Session, though Delhi Police said no formal permission had been sought. Dipke has urged supporters to gather for a night vigil at Jantar Mantar to ensure the march proceeds.

The movement has drawn support from opposition leaders including Rahul Gandhi and Arvind Kejriwal, as well as celebrities such as Hrithik Roshan, Sonakshi Sinha, and Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker. Social activist Anna Hazare has appealed to the government to open talks with the protesters.

Modi's government has blocked CJP's X account, which the group has challenged in a Delhi court. Three students from the All India Students Association who had been fasting alongside Wangchuk for 21 days also require medical attention, organizers said.
